ledger.claim: The trip record confirms the arithmetic independently: the free waiting period of 180 seconds started at 18:33:49 and the driver cancelled at 18:36:46, a served wait of 177 seconds by the platform's own event clock - still short of the 180-second minimum.

The rider's own device was stationary throughout the waiting window - the rider track shows a single distinct speed of 0.0 kph across 48 fixes - which is consistent with a rider waiting at the pickup rather than abandoning it, and it undercuts any suggestion that the rider's absence caused the shortfall.

The amount to be refunded is the cancellation-fee line only: the fare breakdown shows a cancellation_fee of SGD 4.50 and a total_charged of SGD 4.50, with no booking or platform fee on the ledger, so the full contested amount of SGD 4.50 is returned to the rider.

No driver compensation is payable on this outcome: POL-NS-06 provides that where cumulative dwell falls short of the minimum the full refund stands and no driver compensation is payable, and POL-NS-07 compensation is available only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full.

The rider's claim that the driver 'cancelled almost immediately' is not literally accurate - the driver did hold position for nearly the full free period - but the rider's bottom line is correct on the arithmetic: the fee was charged on a wait that fell one second short of the period the fee was consideration for. I do not overstate the rider's account of the timing.

The driver's statement that he 'waited the free period then cancelled' is contradicted by his own trace and by the platform's wait-timer events, which show the cancellation landing before the 180-second period elapsed.

The trip record shows a driver 'arrived' event at 18:33:47 and a wait timer started at 18:33:49, and the driver terminated the trip at 18:36:46 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — a reason code POL-NS-01(d) expressly recognises. Limbs (a) and (d) of the baseline chargeable no-show are therefore satisfied on the platform's own telemetry.

The driver's own GPS trace places him inside the STANDARD arrival radius continuously from 18:33:47 to 18:36:46 — 19 qualifying fixes over a 179-second run, with the trace at 100% coverage and no gaps. That is the in-geofence dwell POL-NS-01(c) requires, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix and not from the arrival tap.

The arrival marker is not false. The trace shows the driver stationary at the pickup pin (min_distance_m 0.0) at the arrival timestamp, not more than 300 m away and not travelling at or above 15 km/h, so POL-NS-05 does not displace the waiting clock and the 179-second dwell stands as computed.

The driver did not sit silent: he sent an in-app message at 18:34:07 reading 'im at the pickup point', delivered at 18:34:08 and read by the rider at 18:34:37, and he cancelled only at 18:36:46 — more than two minutes after the rider read that message. The rider's claim that the driver 'cancelled almost immediately' is contradicted by the record.

The rider's own track never enters the pickup area: 48 rider fixes, zero of them qualifying, with the rider's device sitting 616.9 m to 622.3 m from the pin throughout. The rider was not at the pickup point during the waiting window, which is the factual premise of a no-show fee.

The fare ledger reconciles: the cancellation fee line is SGD 4.50, matching platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd for this trip, with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. There is no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect and no arithmetic basis for a refund.

The driver's payout follows from POL-NS-07: 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 fee in force is SGD 3.60, the residual 20 percent being the platform service fee. The anti-farming check does not trip — no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and 1/62 is far below the 0.08 rate limb — so compensation is payable and the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION.

The rider's own profile shows no_show_disputes_30d of 0 and disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0, so neither POL-NS-09(c) nor POL-NS-09(d) is engaged and there is no repeat-abuse pattern requiring escalation.

The traffic advisory artifact is MISSING — no advisory covers Blk 108 Yishun Ring Rd in this window — so POL-NS-06(i) cannot be run and no accumulation of separate in-geofence intervals is available. I do not assert it; the absence is cited only to record that the limb is unavailable, and the dwell is measured on the single 179-second run.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02741 is refunded to the rider in full, and no compensation is paid to the driver.

Why the charge fails. The free waiting period in force for this STANDARD-zone trip was 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, EV-TRIP-02741). The driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-02741) shows his longest continuous run of qualifying fixes inside the 50 m pickup geofence lasted 179 seconds, from 18:33:47 to 18:36:46 — one second short of the period. POL-NS-06 is strict liability: where the in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period, the fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.

On the driver's case. The trip record does show the 'arrived' event at 18:33:47 and termination at 18:36:46 with reason RIDER_NO_SHOW, so POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) are met. Limb (c) is not: it requires a continuous dwell of at least 180 seconds, and the trace gives 179. The platform's own wait-timer clock agrees in substance — free wait started 18:33:49, cancellation at 18:36:46, a served wait of 177 seconds — so the driver's assertion that he 'waited the free period then cancelled' is contradicted by both his own trace and the platform's events, and his advocate's concession of the 1-second shortfall is consistent with the record. POL-NS-05 does not change this in the driver's favour: his arrival marker was not false (he was at the pin, minimum distance 0.0 m, and not travelling at or above 15 km/h at the arrival timestamp), so the waiting clock is not displaced — but that only confirms the clock the trace already uses, and it does not repair the shortfall. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02741) does reconcile at SGD 4.50 with status CHARGED and refund 0.00, but reconciliation is not the test; the charge still fails on dwell. The rider-track point that the rider's device was stationary does not change the result either; the rider's track in EV-GPS-02741 places the rider roughly 617–622 m from the pin, outside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius, yet POL-NS-06 refunds regardless of rider presence. The rider's phrase 'cancelled almost immediately' is not literally accurate — the driver held position for nearly the full period — but the rider's bottom line is correct on the arithmetic.

On compensation. POL-NS-06 provides that where the cumulative dwell falls short of the minimum the full refund stands and no driver compensation is payable, and POL-NS-07 compensation is available only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, which limb (c) is not. No pin-ambiguity goodwill under POL-NS-03 applies, because the driver's stationary fixes were inside the arrival radius, not between the radius and the 400 m ceiling.

Evidence and confidence. The deciding facts — the 180-second free waiting period and the 179-second dwell — rest on EV-TRIP-02741 and EV-GPS-02741, both admitted as COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with no issue codes, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0; confidence is 0.95. The MISSING traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02741-01 sits at weight 0.0, can carry no fact, and is not relied on.

Referrals and escalation. No referral is produced: the arrival marker was not false, so POL-NS-05(ii) does not fire, and no other clause directs one. No POL-NS-09 trigger is engaged (confidence is above the 0.70 floor, the artifacts agree rather than contradict, the profile counters for repeat abuse and anti-farming are at zero or one, and no deciding fact rests on an impaired artifact). The monetary effect (SGD 4.50) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so the refund executes automatically, subject to the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
